questions.stem: Which of the component of the respiratory chain reacts directly with molecular oxygen?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cyt aa3
  • Present in complex IV of ETC
  • It directly transfers its electrons to oxygen leading to the formation of water



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 124

questions.stem: ETC complexes are formed of protein, enzymes, and a number of metal ions as well as vitamin-derived cofactors. Which of the following vitamin is a component of ETC?
questions.solutionHtml:
Riboflavin
  • In ETC, Complex I (FMN, Fe-S) & Complex II (FAD, Fe-S) are involved, which contains FAD, FMN
  • FAD and FMN are active form of vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
  • Therefore Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) is a component of ETC.

Option C: Nicotinic acid

There are two different questions asked on this, So, BE CAREFUL:

  • Vitamin, which is component of ETC, is Riboflavin as it is present in complex I & II, in the form of FMN & FAD respectively (Figure below).
  • NAD or NADH (made of Nicotinic acid) is not a component of ETC complexes. NADH is just a substrate for ETC complex I (Figure below)
  • So, one can interpret that Vitamins that are used in ETC are both B2 & B3 as FADH2 or NADH can be the starting materials for ETC



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 124, 542

questions.stem: Oxidative phosphorylation involves the generation of ATP by electron flow in ETC. The mechanism involved is called Chemiosmosis coupling with oxidative phosphorylation which can be best defined by:

options.label: A
options.text: Formation of ATP at substrate level

options.label: B
options.text: ATP formation by transport of O2

options.label: C
options.text: ATP generation by pumping of neutron

options.label: D
options.text: ATP generation by pumping of proton

questions.answerText: ATP generation by pumping of proton
questions.solutionHtml:
ATP generation by pumping of proton
  • Chemi-Osmotic coupling of oxidative phosphorylation means ATP is formed when protons that were pumped out during electron transfer are pumped back from intermembrane space back to Mitochondrial Matrix via the F0-F1 complex (see fig).
  • The mechanical energy imparted by this proton pumping is captured in the high-energy P bond of ATP.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No.126

questions.stem: Rotenone is an odorless, colorless, crystalline isoflavone used as a broad-spectrum insecticide, piscicide, and pesticide. It occurs naturally in the seeds and stems of several plants, such as the jicama vine plant, and the roots of several members of Fabaceae. Investigators worked on the mechanism of action of Rotenone on the ETC during ATP synthesis. Rotenone act on which step of the mitochondrial respiratory chain:
questions.solutionHtml:
Complex I to Co-enzyme Q
  • Rotenone works by interfering with the electron transport chain within complex I in mitochondria. It inhibits the transfer of electrons from iron-sulfur centers in complex I to ubiquinone. This interferes with NADH during the creation of usable cellular energy (ATP).
  • Complex I is unable to pass off its electron to CoQ, creating a backup of electrons within the mitochondrial matrix. Other inhibitors of complex I are amobarbital and piercedin A.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 127

questions.stem: Shuttles are required for the transport of NADH generated in the cytoplasm to mitochondria to participate in ETC. If NADH uses a malate shuttle, how many ATPs will be produced?
questions.solutionHtml:
2.5

In Malate shuttle

  • NADH is transported from the cytoplasm to mitochondria.
  • The electrons in the NADH are used to reduce oxaloacetate to Malate by enzyme cytoplasmic MDH.
  • The malate formed is transferred to mitochondria where it is oxidized back to OAA by mitochondrial MDH and electrons are transferred to NAD to form NADH.
  • This NADH enters ETC to give5 ATPs



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 129

questions.stem: The major requirement of cellular energy is met by ATP produced through oxidative phosphorylation which requires the flow of electrons through ETC to oxygen. Which one of the following is a key component of oxidative phosphorylation?

options.label: A
options.text: Using NADH and FAD(H2) to accept electrons as substrates are oxidized.

options.label: B
options.text: A source of electrons, which is usually oxygen in most tissues

options.label: C
options.text: An ATP synthase to synthesize ATP

options.label: D
options.text: An ATP synthetase to synthesize ATP

questions.answerText: An ATP synthase to synthesize ATP
questions.solutionHtml:
An ATP synthase to synthesize ATP
  • The structure of ATP synthase allows the energy of protons moving inside the matrix to be used for ATP synthesis.
  • If protons enter the mitochondria in any way other than through ATP synthase, no ATP can be generated (partial uncoupling).
  • Hence ATP synthase is the most essential component for ATP synthesis.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 126

questions.stem: The inner mitochondrial membrane contains a protein that is a transporter of:
questions.solutionHtml:
ATP

ADP-ATP translocase

  • Present in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
  • helps in the transfer of ATP and ADP molecules across the IMM. It transfers ATP out from the mitochondrial matrix into intermembrane space and on the other hand, it transfers ADP from Intermembrane space into the mitochondria matrix.
  • It uses Flip-Flop Mechanism.
  • Atractyloside inhibits ADP-ATP Translocase.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 128

questions.stem: A young person of age 32 years while working in the agriculture field and spraying 2,4-Dinitrophenol on the crop, accidentally inhaled DNP. The patient was taken to the hospital with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, headache, and giddiness. Emergency symptomatic treatment was started after obtaining a history from the relatives. The probable diagnosis was DNP acute toxicity. True about 2, 4- Dinitrophenol is:

options.label: A
options.text: Prevents ATP synthesis and electron transport chain

options.label: B
options.text: Prevents ATP synthesis and the electron transport chain is increased

options.label: C
options.text: Blocks electron transport chain but ATP synthesis is normal

options.label: D
options.text: Blocks ATP synthesis but the electron transport chain is normal

questions.answerText: Prevents ATP synthesis and the electron transport chain is increased
questions.solutionHtml:
Prevents ATP synthesis and the electron transport chain is increased
  • Here the best answer is that Dinitrophenol prevents ATP synthesis and the electron transport chain (ETC) is increased. Dinitrophenol is an uncoupler.
  • Uncoupler means electron flow (oxidation) is occurring but phosphorylation is not occurring.
  • This will lead to reduced ATP formation as phosphorylation is not occurring.
  • It will stimulate electron transport in order to produce more ATPs.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 127

questions.stemHtml: See the image and tell which complexes are involved when FADH2 enters ETC:
questions.solutionHtml:
Complex II, III, IV

When NADH enters ETC, then the complexes involved are complex I, III, and IV.

But if FADH2 enters ETC, then the complexes involved are complex II, III, and IV.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 124

questions.stem: The shuttle used for the transport of NADH, produced in the cytoplasm into mitochondria for ETC, will decide how quickly and what number of ATPs will be produced from these NADH. Keeping that in mind we can say that Glycerol-P-shuttle is preferred in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Brain and Skeletal muscle
  • Glycerol-P-shuttle is a shorter shuttle (see att. Mantra) and provides lesser but a quick source of ATPs as compared to the Malate shuttle.
  • So, it is present in the brain & skeletal muscles, where energy is needed quickly in case of an emergency.

 




Lehninger Principle of Biochemistry 7th Edition Page No. 687

questions.stem: Which of the following about the electron transport chain are CORRECT?a. It is located in the inner mitochondrion membraneb. Cytochrome C accepts electrons from complex IIc. Complex I is called NADH dehydrogenased. Coenzyme Q accepts electrons from complex I and complex IISelect the correct answer from the given below code:

options.label: B
options.text: If a and d are correct

options.label: C
options.text: If a, c and, d are correct

options.label: D
options.text: If all four (a, b, c, & d) are correct

questions.answerText: If a, c and, d are correct
questions.solutionHtml:
If a, c and, d are correct

It is located in the inner mitochondrion membrane

  • The major components of ETC are located in IMM.
  • There are four fixed protein complexes (Complex I-IV) embedded in the membrane.
  • There are two soluble electron carriers CoQ and Cyt c
  • The CoQ moves freely in the membrane
  • Cyt c is present in the intermembrane space

Complex I is called NADH dehydrogenase

  • Complex I has FMN and Fe-S centers with NADH dehydrogenase enzyme activity.
  • It takes electrons from NADH (get oxidized) and transfers them to ubiquinone (gets reduced), hence is called NADH-Q oxidoreductase.

Coenzyme Q accepts electrons from complex I and complex II

  • Ubiquinone or Q is a movable electron carrier and accepts electrons from both complex I (NADH) and complex II (FADH2)
  • It can accept either one or two electrons at a time.

Cytochrome C accepts electrons from complex II

  • Cytochrome c accepts electrons from complex III and not from complex II
  • It transfers electrons to complex IV.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 124

questions.stem: Arrange the components of ETC used in sequence when ETC starts from FADH2:A. ATP synthaseB. Cytochrome c ReductaseC. Succinate dehydrogenaseD. Cytochrome c oxidaseSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
C → B→ D→ A
  • Succinate Dehydrogenase: part of complex II and oxidizes succinate to fumarate
  • Cyt c reductase: Part of complex III and oxidizes CoQ and reduces cyt c
  • Cyt c oxidase: Part of complex IV and oxidizes Cyt c and reduces O2.
  • ATP synthase: aka complex V and causes phosphorylation of ADP to ATP by using electrochemical energy of H+ gradient across IMM.
  • FADH2  → Succinate Dehydrogenase → Cyt c reductase → Cyt c oxidase → ATP synthase




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition Page No. 75

questions.stem: Which of the following is a physiological uncoupler of oxidative phosphorylation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thermogenin

Uncoupler: Thermogenin

  • Uncoupler means electron flow (oxidation) is occurring but phosphorylation is not occurring.
  • This will lead to reduced ATP formation as phosphorylation is not occurring.
  • Thermogenin, a protein present in brown fat, is a natural/physiological uncoupler of ETC. It is responsible for non-shivering thermogenesis by the release of heat in ETC (see fig).




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 127

questions.stem: Electron flow in the ETC is governed by the difference in the reduction potential of its components. Which of the following set of components has minimum redox potential?
questions.solutionHtml:
NAD+/NADH
  • Redox potential tells about the tendency of a substance to gain electrons and get reduced. In ETC:
  • NAD+/NADH has minimum redox potential (can lose electrons readily)
  • Oxygen has maximum redox potential (can accept electrons very fast)
  • As you go down in ETC, redox potential increases i.e. Complex I < Complex II < Coenzyme Q < Complex III.

 

 




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 116, table 12.1

questions.stem: MELAS inhibit all ETC Complexes EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
II
  • MELAS (mitochondrial encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke) occurs due to a mutation in the mitochondrial genome affecting the enzymes and protein encoded by mtDNA.
  • 13 genes of mtDNA encode the following subunits of ETC: seven for complex I, one for complex III, three for complex IV, and two for complex V (ATP synthase).
  • Complex II and the remaining subunits of ETC are encoded in nuclear DNA
  • So, MELAS inhibits complex I, III & IV of ETC but does not affect complex II.
  • ETC is affected, the brain is affected and due to anaerobic metabolism, lactic acidosis occurs.
  • MELAS is also Involved in Alzheimer’s disease and diabetes mellitus.

 

 




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 130

questions.stem: A child of a farming family has accidentally ingested a pest control agent containing cyanide as one of the major components. He was immediately rushed to a hospital by her parents. The TCA compound which will get depleted first is which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
NAD
  • Cyanide inhibits complex IV of ETC. Cyanide is probably the most potent inhibitor of ETC. It exerts its effect by binding to Fe3+ of cytochrome oxidase (Complex IV) and blocking its function.
  • As ETC is involved in the oxidation of the majority of cellular NADH to regenerate NAD. So, if ETC is inhibited, NADH accumulates. If NADH accumulates, it means NAD is So, TCA is affected because each TCA cycle requires 3 NAD (for Isocitrate Dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and Malate Dehydrogenase).



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 127

questions.stem: ETC consists of a series of protein complexes embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Which of the following is the only non-protein member of ETC?
questions.solutionHtml:
CoQ

ETC has:

  • five protein complexes- Complex I to V
  • two mobile electron carriers – CoQ (ubiquinone) and Cyt c
  • All complexes and cytochrome c are proteins except CoQ
  • Coenzyme Q
    • not a protein
    • hydrophobic, lipophilic compound
    • made up of isoprene units
    • present within the inner mitochondrial membrane.
    • anti-oxidant

 

 




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 122-124

questions.stem: If aerobic glycolysis uses a malate shuttle, how many net ATPs are produced from glycolysis/glucose?
questions.solutionHtml:
7 ATP
  • When the malate shuttle is used for NADH transport, NADH is produced inside the mitochondria give rise to 2.5 ATP via ETC.
  • So the Net ATP yield, in that case, would be 7 ATP

5 ATP

  • The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to NADH. Therefore, the NADH produced in the cytosol cannot directly enter the mitochondria. It enters mitochondria indirectly with the help of shuttles e.g. glycerol phosphate and malate shuttles.
  • In the Glycerol phosphate shuttle, NADH gives rise to FADH2 inside the mitochondrial matrix so 1.5 ATP are formed per NADH.
  • So, net ATP yield is = 5 ATP (see figure below)




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 129

questions.stem: In an incident, 3 workers were killed and two suffered a serious injury, including long-term brain damage at a mushroom growing factory. Workers operated on the valve to a pipe in the factor that became clogged. Workers took a long time to repair the valve in the narrow space without proper ventilation. Investigator concluded the presence of hydrogen sulfide gas that workers inhaled while working in the narrow space that lead to sulfide poisoning. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: H2S inhibits the activity of cytochrome oxidase C enzyme in ETC

options.label: B
options.text: Increased reduction of O2 by protons into the water in ETC

options.label: C
options.text: Inhibit Fe-Cu site in cytochrome oxidase C enzyme

questions.answerText: Increased reduction of O2 by protons into the water in ETC
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased reduction of O2 by protons into the water in ETC
  • Hydrogen sulfide is a highly toxic gas that can produce extremely rapid CNS and respiratory depression. It is also an irritant affecting the skin and mucous membranes. There is no proven antidote for hydrogen sulfide poisoning.
  • Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is responsible for many incidents of occupational toxic exposure, Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an important brain, lung, and nose toxicant. Inhibition of cytochrome oxidase C is the primary biochemical effect associated with lethal H2S exposure.
  • Injury due to H2S exposure occurs primarily by inhalation. Once absorbed, the compound is distributed in the blood and taken up by the brain, liver, kidney, pancreas, and small intestines.
  • Sulfur compounds are severely irritating to the respiratory tract, leading to rhinorrhea, sneezing, sore throat, wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, hemoptysis, and a feeling of suffocation.
  • Sulfur compounds can cause leucopenia and neutropenia as well as cardiac injury with the elevation of troponin I and creatine kinase. The mechanism of H2S toxicity is related to the inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation, which causes a decrease in the available cellular energy.

 




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 127

questions.stem: Oligomycins are macrolides created by Streptomyces that can be poisonous to other organisms. Investigator studied the possible mode of action of oligomycin molecule on the experimental rats. Investigators reported the death of rats administered with oligomycin. He found ATP synthesis in rats was inhibited. Select the incorrect?

options.label: C
options.text: Reduce electron flow through the electron transport chain

options.label: D
options.text: Has no action on the F1 subunit of the proton channel

questions.solutionHtml:
Activating proton channel, F0 subunit
  • Oligomycin A inhibits the activity of the proton channel, F0 subunit in ETC.
  • Oligomycin A is an inhibitor of ATP synthase. In oxidative phosphorylation research, it is used to prevent state 3 (phosphorylating) respiration. Oligomycin A inhibits ATP synthase by blocking its proton channel (F0 subunit), which is necessary for oxidative phosphorylation of ADP to ATP (energy production).
  • The inhibition of ATP synthesis by oligomycin A will significantly reduce electron flow through the electron transport chain; however, electron flow is not stopped completely due to a process known as proton leak or mitochondrial uncoupling.
  • This process is due to the facilitated diffusion of protons into the mitochondrial matrix through an uncoupling protein such as thermogenin, or UCP1.

 




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 127
